solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: The work of Johnson, say, or that of Pepys, embracing new tonic (10)

indicatorNotes.embracing: DIARY holds the other letters inside it
indicatorNotes.new: the letters of TONIC are made new, rearranged

blocks.note: Samuel Pepys is famous for his diary

annotation.surface: A comparison of two famous English writers' great works.
annotation.walkthrough: Samuel Johnson compiled the great 1755 dictionary of English; 'say' marks him as one example of a lexicographer. Pepys was a 17th-century London diarist.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Johnson's most famous work is his Dictionary of the English Language.

entries.clue: Meaning to dine in, if working (10)

indicatorNotes.working: the letters are put to work, set in motion into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone meaning to eat at home if their job allows.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Meaning' reads as a verb (intending) but is the noun definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what a dictionary gives for each word is its sense.

entries.clue: My chef isn’t finished (3)

indicatorNotes.isn’t finished: the word is left without its final letter

blocks.note: COOK loses its last letter K

annotation.surface: Someone complaining that their cook is still at work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive but is the exclamation of surprise, as is 'Coo!', an old-fashioned British expression of astonishment.
annotation.definitionFit: Both 'My!' and 'Coo!' are exclamations of surprise.

entries.clue: At home, drink one had is tasteless (7)

blocks.note: a sip is a small drink
had shortens to 'd, as in I'd

annotation.surface: A verdict on a drink someone had at home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Had' giving D comes from contractions like I'd = I had.
annotation.definitionFit: Insipid food or drink lacks flavour: it is tasteless.

entries.clue: Most modern and cosy home we must visit (6)

indicatorNotes.must visit: WE go inside NEST, as a visitor goes inside a home

blocks.note: a nest is a cosy home
used as is, placed inside NE…ST

annotation.surface: A sales pitch for a brand-new cosy house worth a visit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'We' is used unchanged; the surface makes it sound like the house-hunters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both superlatives mean the most recent.

entries.clue: Dance and drink with graduate (5)

blocks.note: BA = Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

annotation.surface: A graduation celebration with dancing and drinking.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a graduation party, so 'Dance' and 'drink' look like two activities rather than a definition and a piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the Cuban ballroom rhythm is one kind of dance.

entries.clue: Veteran fighter with arrow he’s shot (8)

indicatorNotes.shot: the letters are shot to pieces and reassembled

annotation.surface: An old soldier with an arrow he has fired.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shot' reads as the arrow being fired, but it is the anagram indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: An old warhorse is a veteran who has seen many battles.

entries.clue: Clean one’s teeth, having fluorine deprivation (5)

blocks.note: F is the chemical symbol for fluorine

annotation.surface: Dental advice about teeth deprived of fluoride.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all dentistry, which makes fluorine look like part of the story rather than a single letter.
annotation.definitionFit: To floss is to clean between one's teeth with thread.

entries.clue: Australian native without means initially to play cricket (6)

blocks.note: w/o is the written shorthand for without
to bat is to play cricket

annotation.surface: An Australian who cannot afford a game of cricket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Australian native' suggests a person, but it is an animal native to Australia.
annotation.definitionFit: The wombat is a burrowing marsupial native to Australia.

entries.clue: Extremely useful to put in reliable senior doctor (10)

indicatorNotes.Extremely: take the extremes, the outer letters, of 'useful'

blocks.note: first and last letters of useful, placed inside CONS…TANT

annotation.surface: Praise for a dependable senior doctor who is very useful.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' reads as 'very' but asks for the ends of 'useful'. In British hospitals a consultant is the most senior grade of doctor.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: in the British NHS this is the title of the top grade of hospital specialist.

entries.clue: Final goal (3)

blocks.note: final as in an amount left after all deductions
in football, the mesh behind the posts stands for the goal

annotation.surface: The deciding goal in a cup final.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests football's final match, but 'Final' is an adjective, as in a net result.
annotation.definitionFit: Net means final, as in net profit; and in football the net stands for the goal.

entries.clue: Send message to reserve standard publication (8)

blocks.note: to text someone is to send them a message

annotation.surface: An instruction to message someone to reserve a standard book.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one errand; the split falls after 'Send message to'.
annotation.definitionFit: A textbook is the standard published work on a subject.

entries.clue: Nut I chop as it’s cracked (9)

indicatorNotes.cracked: the letters are broken open and rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone chopping a nut as its shell cracks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cracked' fits nuts so well it looks like part of the scene rather than the anagram indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the green-kernelled seed is one kind of nut.

entries.clue: US DJ receiving kiss in Tuesday party (6)

indicatorNotes.receiving: to receive is to take in, so TUE takes X inside itself

blocks.note: x is a kiss at the end of a letter, placed inside TU…E

annotation.surface: An American radio DJ getting a kiss at a Tuesday party.
annotation.walkthrough: DJ looks like a disc jockey but means dinner jacket, the British name for what Americans call a tuxedo.
annotation.definitionFit: A tuxedo is the American word for a dinner jacket.

entries.clue: Tusked creature used to be grabbing large sort of football (6)

indicatorNotes.grabbing: WAS grabs the letters, holding them inside

blocks.note: L = large, as on clothing labels
RU = rugby union, placed with L inside WA…S

annotation.surface: A tusked animal that once grabbed a ball.
annotation.walkthrough: Rugby union is a form of football; its abbreviation RU is standard in crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: The walrus is an Arctic sea mammal with long tusks.

entries.clue: Excellent payment — finally one is solvent! (7)

annotation.surface: Relief at a good payment: at last someone can pay their debts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Solvent' in the surface means able to pay debts; the definition is the chemical sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Acetone is a chemical solvent, used in nail-polish remover.

entries.clue: Puzzle that’s complicated in game (6)

annotation.surface: A tricky puzzle that crops up during a game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Complicated' looks like a description of the puzzle but it is the anagram indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are nouns for something baffling to work out.

entries.clue: No returning the total in one’s account, all things considered (2,7)

indicatorNotes.returning: NO goes back, reading right to left

blocks.note: your balance is the total in your bank account

annotation.surface: A bank refusing to return a customer's savings.
annotation.walkthrough: The banking surface hides an idiom: weighing up both sides of a scale.
annotation.definitionFit: On balance means having weighed everything up, all things considered.

entries.clue: Ancient region seen in early diagram (5)

indicatorNotes.seen in: the answer can be seen inside the next words

annotation.surface: A historical region shown on an early map.
annotation.walkthrough: Lydia was a kingdom in western Anatolia, home of King Croesus.
annotation.definitionFit: Lydia was an ancient region of Asia Minor, now in Turkey.

entries.clue: Evasive person vexedly avoiding odd items (3)

indicatorNotes.avoiding odd items: skip the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters, keeping the even ones

annotation.surface: A slippery person dodging awkward questions in irritation.
annotation.walkthrough: An eel is slippery, so the word is used for a person who is hard to pin down.
annotation.definitionFit: Calling someone an eel means they are slippery and evasive.

entries.clue: Snack to show off on board? (3-3)

blocks.note: surfers' and skiers' slang for performing flashy stunts

annotation.surface: A snack that makes you want to show off aboard ship.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a ship; it is a surfboard or skateboard, where showing off is called hot-dogging.
annotation.definitionFit: The noun is a sausage-in-a-bun snack; the verb is surfing slang for stunting.

entries.clue: A bad actor with Oscar from west US city (5)

indicatorNotes.from west: in an across clue, read from the west, right to left

blocks.note: a ham is a bad, overacting actor
Oscar is O in the NATO alphabet; A HAM O then reversed

annotation.surface: An inept actor landing an Oscar from a western American city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' suggests the film award, but it stands for the letter O.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Nebraska's largest city is one US city.

entries.clue: Cockney cuts audibly — using this? (3)

indicatorNotes.Cockney: a Cockney drops the H, so HACKS becomes 'ACKS
indicatorNotes.audibly: the word is spoken, not written

blocks.note: cuts = hacks; a Cockney drops the H

annotation.surface: A question about what tool a Londoner chops with.
annotation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, famously drop the H at the start of words. The whole clue is also the definition: an axe is what you hack with.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue asks what tool someone hacks with, and the chopping tool fits.

entries.clue: Displayed by nobleman, a gem enticing handling (10)

indicatorNotes.Displayed by: the answer is shown inside the words that follow

annotation.surface: A nobleman showing off a tempting jewel.
annotation.walkthrough: The jewellery surface hides a word for running things; the answer spans three words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns mean the control or running of affairs.
